title: The job that ran at the same time as itself
blurb: Claims were split across commands and re-enqueues let two workers share a job.
prompt: A nightly billing job ran twice concurrently, because a slow worker's visibility timeout re-enqueued the job while the original was still running. A crash mid-claim also lost jobs with no trace. The model-generated draft claims non-atomically. Review it, fix it, and prove claims and returns are atomic.
aiNote: The draft moves a job out of the queue and marks it in-flight in separate writes, so a crash between them evaporates the job, and its timeout return is not atomic with the claim check, so a live slow worker and a fresh claimant can both hold the same job.
testIdea: Kill a worker between claim steps and assert the job is still claimable; simulate a slow worker past its visibility timeout and assert the job cannot be double-claimed; feed a schema-invalid payload and assert it dead-letters on the first attempt.
followUps: What visibility timeout fits your slowest job, and how do you measure it?
Should the dead-letter queue be replayable, and with what protections?
How do you make a job's side effects idempotent?
